problems.title: An ordinary-loss prefix has incompatible shapes and indices
problems.source_location: src/utils/train_utils.py, get_scfm_timesteps, lines 24–70; trainer/flux_scfm.py, shortcut target around lines 1523–1610; trainer/sd3_scfm.py, corresponding target
claim: For batch size \(N\), prefix fraction \(r\), prefix size \(m=\lceil Nr\rceil\) and skip \(s\), teacher durations have shape \((N,s)\). The source assigns row zero of their prefix into a length-\(m\) student slice, then returns full-batch teacher/self indices to a closure receiving only the suffix.
analysis: Take \(N=4,r=0.6,s=2\), teacher steps \(32\), teacher ratio \(1\). The assignment attempts a length-\(2\) row into a length-\(3\) slice. With \(r=0.5\), the dimensions happen to agree, isolating the next defect: indices \([0,1,2,3]\) address a suffix of length \(2\). Generally, for \(0<m<N\), index \(N-1\) belongs to one returned branch but exceeds suffix limit \(N-m-1\). No random selection can avoid that union-of-indices contradiction. The paper’s teacher/self mixture is a separate setting and must not be confused with this ordinary-loss prefix.
result: The nonzero-prefix path is invalid. Both supplied launchers set the prefix fraction to zero, so this witness does not establish failure of their training runs.
repair: Assign the first duration column \(d_{0:m}=D_{0:m,0}\), and return suffix-relative lists \(I_T^{\prime}=\{i-m:i\in I_T,i\ge m\}\), with the analogous self list. These disjoint lists cover exactly the suffix; a complete native training repair remains unverified.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: A static shape/index contradiction is established in an exposed branch, while the actual published-launcher controls bypass it.

problems.title: The minimum-step default leaves no self-teaching choice
problems.source_location: src/utils/train_utils.py, lines 35–43; trainer/flux_scfm.py, teacher_min_timesteps parser default; scripts/train_flux_scfm.sh
claim: The self branch samples \(2^j\) with \(1\le j<\lfloor\log_2 n_{\min}\rfloor\). The exposed minimum teacher-step value \(2\) gives an empty range.
analysis: Set skip \(2\), minimum steps \(2\), zero ordinary-loss prefix and teacher ratio \(0\). Then \(\lfloor\log_2 2\rfloor=1\), so the draw is from \(\varnothing\). With the parser’s teacher ratio \(1/2\), the branch merely becomes stochastic; its conditional occurrence probability over \(N\) independent draws is \(1-2^{-N}\). The supplied launchers instead use \(32\) minimum steps and the nonempty set \(\{2,4,8,16\}\).
result: A declared parameter boundary is unusable without a domain guard. The default experimental launchers are unaffected and no FID/timing result is recomputed.
repair: For skip \(2\) and nonzero self probability, require minimum steps at least \(4\), or directly require the constructed candidate set to be nonempty. Other skips need their own range/divisibility conditions.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This is an exposed configuration-validation bug, with explicit counterevidence against attributing it to the paper’s actual launcher settings.

problems.title: A later Flux EMA setting needs experiment correspondence
problems.source_location: Section 5.4, p.9; Appendix E; trainer/flux_scfm.py, fast EMA update
claim: The paper describes fast/slow EMA coefficients \(0.99\) and \(0.999\); the current Flux source sets the fast coefficient to zero.
analysis: The current head is the later commit titled “flux param fix,” while the SD3 branch retains the described coefficients. A zero fast coefficient copies current parameters; it is a different setting, but a later deliberate change does not prove the historical experiments used a wrong coefficient.
result: Checkpoint-specific experiment manifests are required to connect the later release change to a published result. This is not counted as a confirmed paper error.
problems.impact_rationale: Version discrepancy alone does not establish mistaken historical experiments.
